translation:
The workings of time are strange, each moment unlike any other. When Sadguru Shri Jivanji Maharaj founded the Ramkabir tradition, he did not institute any worship of idols or images, nor any form of ritual praise-worship. Yet today, in the sixth generation after Jivanji Maharaj, Narsinhdasji resolved never again to sit upon his own seat, and bowed to it instead. The very seat on which he used to sit daily to hold satsang (holy company) and recite katha-kirtan (discourse and devotional singing), he now bows to again and again, joining both hands, his eyes brimming with tears of love. Streams of tears flow from his eyes. Again and again he falls to his knees in reverence. Bowing with the deepest humility, Narsinhdasji says, "O Maharaj! For the sake of saving the honor of this humble soul, you had to endure so much hardship! You came for my sake! Sitting upon this very seat, you proved me innocent! Now I shall never sit upon this seat again."

This incident took place in Puniyad on Shravan Sud 14 of Vikram Samvat 1872. What had happened was this: Narsinhdas had taken Vasanti and left her at the home of the Thakor of Zulana, where she lived happily with her son. But the very wicked man of Puniyad who had earlier committed misconduct with Vasanti shamelessly demanded her again. Narsinhdasji counselled him firmly and advised him to restrain his lust. This only provoked him further, and he lodged a complaint with the Maharaja of the Baroda state, alleging that this Narsinhdas, posing as a preceptor of the Uda sect, had run away with Vasanti and had killed both her and her son. The Diwan of the Gaekwad government thereupon instructed his Subha (governor) to go to Puniyad in person, investigate, and submit a report.

Troubled by the thought that officials of the Gaekwad government would come to his own home to investigate, that all manner of questions would be asked, and what face he would then show to society, Narsinhdasji left his house before the Subha arrived. He returned in the evening, and the devotees of the village along with the leading Patels came to congratulate him. Narsinhdasji could not understand why, but as he was entering the house, he noticed a streak of light vanishing from above his seat, and beside the seat he found a letter from Shri Vishaji Kashiji, the Subha of the Gaekwad government, declaring him innocent.

He then grasped the full meaning of what had happened: that while he was away, the merciful Lord (Krupanath) himself had come and taken his place, bearing witness and proving him innocent. Overcome, with streams of loving tears in his eyes, he began bowing again and again to that seat.
